patient_data.chief_complaint: Persistent cough and fever for 5 days

imaging_study.description: Chest X-ray PA and Lateral views
imaging_study.indication: Fever, cough, dyspnea - rule out pneumonia
imaging_study.findings: There is a focal opacity in the right lower lobe consistent with consolidation measuring approximately 6 x 4 cm. Air bronchograms are visible within the consolidation. No pleural effusion identified. Heart size is normal (cardiothoracic ratio <0.5). No pneumothorax. No mediastinal widening. Left lung is clear. Costophrenic angles are sharp bilaterally. No rib fractures.
imaging_study.impression: Right lower lobe pneumonia. Clinical correlation recommended.

lab_results.notes: Elevated white blood cell count indicating infection

clinical_notes.title: Emergency Department Triage Note
clinical_notes.content: 60 y/o male presents to ED with c/o cough x 5 days, fever (max 39.2°C), and SOB. Reports productive cough with yellow sputum, chills, night sweats. Denies CP (except pleuritic), hemoptysis. PMH: HTN, HLD. Meds: Lisinopril, Atorvastatin. NKDA except PCN allergy (rash). VS: T 38.7, BP 128/82, HR 98, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA. Patient appears acutely ill with mild respiratory distress. PRIORITY: Urgent.

clinical_notes.title: History and Physical Examination
clinical_notes.content:
Chief Complaint: Cough and fever for 5 days

HPI: Mr. Johnson is a 60 y/o male with PMH of HTN and HLD who presents with 5 days of productive cough with yellow sputum, fever (max 39.2°C), and progressive dyspnea. Associated symptoms include chills, night sweats, decreased appetite, and pleuritic chest pain. Denies hemoptysis, leg swelling, recent travel, or sick contacts.

PMH: Hypertension (well-controlled), Hyperlipidemia
Medications: Lisinopril 10mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg daily
Allergies: Penicillin (rash)
SH: Never smoker, occasional EtOH, works as accountant, lives with wife

Physical Examination:
Vitals: T 38.7°C, BP 128/82, HR 98, RR 22, SpO2 94% on RA
General: Alert, oriented x3, appears acutely ill, mild respiratory distress
Respiratory: Decreased breath sounds RLL, dullness to percussion RLL, bronchial breathing, inspiratory crackles
Cardiovascular: RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmurs
Other systems: Unremarkable

clinical_notes.title: Progress Note - Day 1
clinical_notes.content:
60 y/o male admitted with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), right lower lobe.

Subjective: Patient reports continued cough and fever. Feels "very tired". Appetite remains poor. Denies worsening dyspnea.

Objective:
Vitals: T 38.2°C (improved), BP 125/78, HR 92, RR 20, SpO2 96% on 2L NC
Physical: Decreased breath sounds RLL persist, crackles unchanged
Labs: WBC 13.8 (↓ from 14.5), CRP pending
CXR: Reviewed - RLL consolidation as previously described

Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia, improving
CURB-65: 0 (low risk)

Plan:
1. Continue Ceftriaxone 2g IV daily + Azithromycin 500mg IV daily
2. Maintain O2 to keep SpO2 >92%
3. IV fluids at 100 mL/hr
4. Incentive spirometry q2h while awake
5. Recheck labs tomorrow AM
6. Repeat CXR in 48h
7. Monitor for clinical improvement
8. DVT prophylaxis with enoxaparin
9. Plan to transition to PO antibiotics if improved

Disposition: Continue inpatient care

diagnostic_query.query: Generate comprehensive diagnostic assessment for patient with fever, productive cough, dyspnea, and right lower lobe opacity on chest X-ray. Elevated WBC and inflammatory markers. Assess for pneumonia and provide differential diagnoses.
diagnostic_query.clinical_notes: 60-year-old male with 5-day history of productive cough, fever (max 39.2°C), dyspnea, and pleuritic chest pain. Physical exam shows decreased breath sounds in right lower lobe with dullness to percussion. Chest X-ray demonstrates right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms. Laboratory results show WBC 14.5, CRP 85, procalcitonin 2.5 (all elevated). SpO2 94% on room air. CURB-65 score: 0. No significant past medical history except controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
